title: Five Winters and One Short Receipt
subtitle: 经济消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通）
meta: 主题语境：经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通）　|　核心词汇：fee　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fee 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 my father ① paid a fee that no clerk in the office would have recorded, and he said the paying was the whole of the winter. The ② fee, meaning the charge itself and not the bill, ran five winters and stayed unrecorded in the book; a fee, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ fee in that office had the same short receipt beside it, and the ④ fee at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the course and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A fee, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; my father said the recording is the part that fills five winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the fee was the whole of the year, meaning the cost and not the charge. The ⑥ fee, meaning the cost and not any of that, is the only thing in a year that everybody waits for and nobody records; fee, he said, is either something you pay or the only word that means both a charge and a cost. He said the cost is the part they remember.

By 1974 the ⑦ fee had become a line in a ledger, and the ledger had become an argument about the short receipt. The ⑧ fee of the whole thing, my father wrote in January, was one office and five winters of recording; fee, he said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ fee I remember is the one recorded in the ledger, which closed in 1976 and is still described as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ fee, my mother said in 1978, is the only one that improves by being recorded; every fee, she said, is a cost that has agreed to look like a charge. She said the cost was the honest half.

task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 费用；收费（指办公室里每一笔旁边的那一笔）
B. n. 费用（指那一笔本身，与账单相对）
C. 固定搭配：pay a fee 付一笔费用
D. n. 费用（指留给课程的那一笔）

F. n. 费用（指账本上写到、被记下的那一笔）
G. n. 代价；花费（指一年里人人都等却无人记下的那样东西）
H. n. 代价（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人记下的那样东西）

answers.why: pay a fee 意为“付一笔费用”，1969 年父亲付了一笔办公室里没有一位办事员肯记下的费用。
fee 意为“费用”，指那一笔本身而不是账单，它经过了五个冬天而在簿子上没有记号。
fee 意为“费用”，指办公室里每一笔旁边的那一笔，每一笔旁边都有同一张短短的收据。
fee 意为“费用”，指留给课程的那一笔，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
fee 意为“代价、花费”，指一年里人人都等却无人记下的那样东西，叔叔说这份花费就是那一年的全部。
fee 意为“代价”，指人人都等却无人记下的那样东西而不是那一笔费用，是一年里人人都等、却无人记下的东西。
fee 意为“费用”，指账本上写到、被记下的那一笔，到 1974 年这一笔成了账本里的一行。
fee 意为“费用”，父亲一月写道，整件事的收费之事是一间办公室和五个冬天的记下。
fee 意为“费用”，我记得的是账本上记下的那一笔，1976 年结束了，至今仍被说成办公室里最安静的一笔。
fee 为抽象总称，母亲 1978 年说，一笔费用是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的东西。
